title: Braves’ Hurston Waldrep, Spencer Schwellenbach to have season-ending surgeries
content:
ATLANTA — Friday evening before the series opener against the Colorado Rockies, it was announced that two Atlanta Braves pitchers who could’ve been assets for the club this season will undergo season-ending surgery.

Right-hander Hurston Waldrep will have Tommy John surgery, and right-hander Spencer Schwellenbach will have surgery to repair his right elbow, which was fractured in 2025. The dates for both procedures have not been announced.

“(They were) following the protocol that was laid out by the doctors that they’ve been seeing,” manager Walt Weiss said. “We’ve gotten multiple opinions from the best doctors in the country, and we’re following their advice. It just gets to a point where they probably hit their threshold for their injuries, and that’s when things flare up.”

Waldrep, who missed the beginning of the season with elbow surgery in February to remove loose bodies and didn’t make his season debut with the Braves until June 26, went on the 7-day Triple-A injured list on July 21 after being pulled from his start. He had been consulting with multiple experts about the next steps, but on Aug. 10 it was announced that he would be heading to the team’s North Port, Fla. complex to begin their throwing program.

According to a Braves spokesperson, Waldrep felt discomfort and after getting an MRI, surgery was highly recommended. The Braves’ first-round pick in the 2023 draft likely won’t be seen until 2028.

Schwellenbach had been rehabbing mostly in North Port most of the season after missing the majority of 2025 with a fractured right elbow. He pitched four bullpen sessions and eventually returned to Truist Park to throw in front of the coaching staff. He went back to Florida during this past month, feeling a flare-up in the same elbow during his rehab process.

The Braves have dealt with injuries to their starters all season, and there was hope, especially before the Aug. 3 trade deadline, that Waldrep and Schwellenbach could contribute.

Despite that, the Braves’ rotation has the fourth-lowest starter ERA (3.58) heading into Friday after Chris Sale’s shutout. They are operating with a six-man rotation that includes Sale, Grant Holmes, Bryce Elder, Martin Pérez, AJ Smith-Shawver and Tyler Mahle, their lone starter added at the trade deadline. In addition, Reynaldo López, who was in the starting rotation before going on the injured list with left knee inflammation, will throw his second rehab start for Triple-A Gwinnett in Louisville.

So as tough as it is to lose both pitchers, the Braves are theoretically covered for the rest of this season.

Right-hander Spencer Strider also went down to Florida when Waldrep began his throwing progression, but no update was provided on him. The 2023 All-Star has been sidelined since June 13 with right shoulder inflammation after leaving a start against the Mets when his velocity noticeably dropped.

“That window is getting smaller,” Weiss said of Strider’s timeline. “You just start to run out of time, (but) wouldn’t rule it out, but I’d say long shot.”
